question: does InterPro, annotating the same sequences with its own profiles, agree that they carry a Rieske domain?

independence.independent: given a sequence, whether InterPro places a Rieske domain on it. Those profiles were built by other people, from other data, at other thresholds
independence.not_independent: which sequences get asked. The candidate pool was selected with this project's own Rieske and motif models, so InterPro cannot object to a sequence we never included
independence.therefore: this measures precision, and says nothing at all about recall: the sequences we missed are outside it

denominators.why_the_rest_are_excluded: a sequence InterPro has not annotated does not contradict us, it is unannotated -- most are recent unreviewed entries. An absence of evidence is not evidence of absence

interpro_sees_rieske_we_do_not.why_this_is_not_a_contradiction: InterPro's measure is profile similarity -- is a Rieske domain present -- while ours is whether the four cluster ligands are in place. A Rieske fold without its cluster cannot do the chemistry, so the gate asks for the ligands. The two statements are different, not opposed
interpro_sees_rieske_we_do_not.why_it_is_published_anyway: these sequences are dropped by the gate, and a drop that nobody can see is the failure mode this database keeps finding. 76 of the 139 carry all three mononuclear iron ligands, which makes them a set a curator should look at: a substituted cluster ligand with an intact catalytic triad

family_entries_are_not_errors: InterPro's separate family names -- cholesterol 7-desaturase, pheophorbide a oxygenase, vanillate O-demethylase, 3-ketosteroid 9-alpha-monooxygenase -- are not disagreements. This database collects Rieske oxygenases as a whole rather than ring-hydroxylating dioxygenases alone, and those names are what that breadth looks like from the outside
